Definition: properly, to put in commotion; by implication, to disturb, drive, destroy
BiblicalUsage: To put an army in commotion is to throw it into confusion, and that is what God does to his enemies. He troubled the Egyptians in Exodus 14:24, he discomfited the Amorites before Joshua in Joshua 10:10, and David sings in Psalms 18:14 and 2 Samuel 22:15 that God shot out his arrows and scattered them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the confusion of the enemy is God's own work, not mine to arrange. When the battle is the Lord's, the other side falls apart before it ever reaches me.
RelatedEvents: The Exodus and the Red Sea
